hero.title: File:Flynn Creek Impact Crater marker 20260315.jpg
hero.description:
Flynn Creek Impact Crater marker along Flynn Creek Road, Jackson County, Tennessee.  The text says:
Over 560 million years ago, an asteroid or comet struck this area and more than 10 miles/second forming a crater 2.5 mlles across and, in seconds, ejecting 0.3 cubic mile of rock. Deformed limestone beds seen in adjacent cliffs were violently upllfted to form a shattered central peak.  This crater, now buried beneath younger rocks, was used by NASA/USGS in training Apollo astronauts and represents an Important class of craters found on other planets and satellltes in our solar system.

gallery.title: File:Flynn Creek crater AR1VDUT00030114.jpg
gallery.description: Approximate location of Flynn Creek impact crater, Tennessee.  Location is based on a figure in "Flynn Creek Impact Structure: New Insights from Breccias, Melt Features, Shatter Cones, and Remote Sensing," 2004, by J. C. Evenick, Pascal Lee, and Bethany Deane.  Air photo is dated April 21, 1975.  The crater is buried by later sediments and is not obvious on the surface.
categories: Impact craters of the United States

gallery.title: File:Flynn Creek Road outcrop 20260315.jpg
gallery.description: Outcrop of Stones River Group of Ordovician Limestone along Flynn Creek Road, at the center of the Flynn Creek crater structure, Jackson County, Tennessee.  The rocks dip at roughly 30 degrees unlike all other rocks 2 miles or more away which are flat-lying.  Faults are also present in this photo.
